topic: Deep ecosystem rendering and 100x100 field optimization
currentUserGoal: Make the ecosystem prototype feel fast and fluid now while preserving a genuinely scalable path to a 100x100 field with 10,000 logical tiles.
workCompleted: Profiled the actual ecosystemPrototype route instead of the obsolete legacy performance harness at 1x1, 32x32, 100x100, phone size, near zoom, and with all eight helpers active.
Replaced timer-polled field redraws with dirty-chunk-driven rendering and coalesced UI refreshes onto deterministic production ticks or accepted input actions.
Stopped advanceEcosystem from scanning chunk dirtiness on rendered frames that did not execute a fixed production tick.
Moved tile and ambient animation metadata out of Phaser DataManager lookups and into fixed typed arrays, and reduced near-tile sway to one trigonometric calculation per tile.
Replaced the touch cooldown Graphics clear-and-rebuild path with four persistent pooled display objects while preserving blocked, recovering, and ready feedback.
Added bounded touch-impact and helper-effect budgets for phone and distant field LODs.
Made displayed HP predict deterministic damage within the current fixed-tick window so the bar moves continuously without changing simulation outcomes.

Skipped hidden-field animation work and idle heartbeat display writes, requested a high-performance WebGL context for the ecosystem prototype, and exposed actually visible display-object counts in the redesign harness.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 132 Vitest tests across 18 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
Idle 1x1 field redraws fell from five to six polls per second to zero when no chunks changed; visible field objects were approximately 48 to 49.

A 100x100 field used 10,000 logical tiles in 11,700 compact bytes, rendered 100 chunk summaries, performed zero full-field scans, and showed approximately 156 visible objects on the 390x844 phone viewport.
The 100x100 field with all eight helpers active showed approximately 198 to 203 visible objects, three to seven active effects, and nine to fourteen active tweens while production continued.
Near zoom on a 32x32 field rendered 165 individual tiles from a bounded pool and showed approximately 222 visible objects.

The browser harness reported about 144 FPS and a 6.75 ms p95 frame delta in ordinary, helper-heavy, phone-sized, and near-zoom checks on the current test machine; simulation work stayed around 0.001 to 0.01 ms and no browser warnings or errors appeared.

release.status: Verified local optimization checkpoint; not pushed, merged into master, or promoted to production.

currentGitStatus: The optimization implementation, tests, and this handoff are intended for one local commit on codex/ecosystem-factory-prototype.
docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md remains an unrelated untracked file and must stay untouched unless the user explicitly requests it.
The local Vite server remains available at http://127.0.0.1:5173.
knownIssues: The browser measurements establish bounded work and strong headroom on the current machine; they do not replace hands-on testing on the user's slowest target phone or tablet.
Display pools remain allocated after zooming back out, but hidden pooled objects do not animate or render and their counts remain capped by viewport policy.
The playtest debug controls can obscure mobile UI and are not representative of the normal player route.
The current 100x100 far view is intentionally a 10x10 chunk summary rather than 10,000 simultaneous sprites.
nextRecommendedSteps: Have the user replay the first run and judge perceived input latency, cooldown clarity, and HP motion on their own display.
Add a repeatable low-power redesign benchmark mode only when testing on slower hardware reveals a measurable miss.
Continue the visible Field Mouse production-chain objective after the hands-on smoothness check.
doNotRevert: Keep 10,000 logical tiles separate from the bounded near, mid, and far display pools.
Keep field redraws dirty-chunk-driven; do not restore a per-frame or fixed polling redraw loop.
Keep simulation deterministic and fixed-tick-based; displayed HP prediction must remain visual only.
Do not use the legacy 1,200-tile harness as evidence for ecosystemPrototype performance.
Keep touch feedback pooled and effect counts bounded by viewport and LOD.
